approved: Criminal Code and Other Legislation Amendment (Removing Commonwealth Restrictions on Cannabis) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let state and territory governments decide whether to legalise and regulate cannabis.
It would stop federal regulations and ministerial decisions from listing cannabis as a controlled or border controlled substance.
The changes would take effect one year after the bill receives royal assent.
Removes cannabis from lists of controlled and border controlled drugs, plants and precursors in Commonwealth criminal law.
Excludes cannabis from offences for importing psychoactive substances and from the definition of narcotic drugs under the Crimes (Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances) Act 1990.
Repeals regulations that list cannabis as a controlled plant and removes related definitions from the Defence Force Discipline Act 1982.
State and territory governments, adults who use cannabis, and Commonwealth law enforcement agencies.
